question: Which statement best describes Block axis vs inline axis?
options: Logical properties are defined relative to two axes. The inline axis is the direction text flows within a line (left-to-right in English, right-to-left in Arabic); the block axis is the direction lines stack (top-to-bottom in horizontal writing modes). 'start' and 'end' refer to where each axis begins and ends. In a default LTR horizontal document, inline-start = left, inline-end = right, block-start = top, block-end = bottom.

Borders have logical equivalents too: border-block-start, border-inline-end, etc., plus their -width/-style/-color longhands. This is how you put a leading-edge accent border that stays on the correct side in RTL. border-inline-start-width is the logical version of 'the border at the start of the line', i.e. left in LTR and right in RTL.

margin-block and margin-inline (and padding-block/padding-inline) are two-value shorthands for the block and inline axes, each with -start and -end longhands. margin-inline: auto centers a block horizontally in LTR, and stays correct in RTL. They replace pairs of physical properties (margin-top/bottom, margin-left/right) with direction-aware equivalents.

For positioned elements, inset is the logical shorthand replacing top/right/bottom/left, with inset-block, inset-inline, and longhands like inset-inline-start. inset: 0 stretches an absolutely positioned element to all edges. inset-inline-start: 0 pins it to the start edge, which flips appropriately in RTL — unlike left: 0 which is always physically left.

question: Which statement best describes margin / padding -block and -inline?
options: writing-mode (horizontal-tb, vertical-rl, vertical-lr) sets the block axis orientation, and direction (ltr/rtl) sets the inline axis direction. Together they define how logical properties map to physical sides. Setting dir="rtl" on the html element (or direction: rtl) makes inline-start become the right side, so logical CSS mirrors the layout automatically. text-align: start/end are the logical text alignments.

question: Which statement best describes inset and logical positioning?
options: With logical properties, a single stylesheet supports LTR and RTL (and vertical scripts) without duplicate [dir=rtl] override rules. You stop writing margin-left for 'leading space' and instead use margin-inline-start, which automatically moves to the right in Arabic/Hebrew. This eliminates an entire class of mirroring bugs and shrinks the CSS needed to ship globally.
